open_points.subject: OwnerFormField identity
open_points.text: one field of the owner's pages
open_points.question: Is a field occurrence on each page a distinct OwnerFormField, or do equal names across pages denote one shared field; and, if page membership distinguishes them, must the page or owner action be a fact of the model?
options: Each page occurrence is distinct and page/action membership is a fact
Equal field definitions across pages are one shared value
Field names are globally unique, so page membership is unnecessary
open_points.default_guess: Treat each page occurrence as distinct and add its page or owner action to the facts.

witness.initial: The create-project page and correct-customer page both contain an input named `name` with the same scope and reading kind.
events: The data provider adds both inputs to the owner form table.
The owner interface renders and reads both pages.
outcomes: The two rows are the same value because all declared facts are equal.
The rows are distinct because they belong to different pages.
witness.observer: The owner interface implementer sees whether one definition can be changed independently of the other.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField location
open_points.text:
Facts: the field's name; whether it belongs to the request or to its values;
how its text is read.
open_points.question: What fact identifies the precise location that the field reads or fills, including nested members and tuple positions, now that path and tuple-position facts are absent?
options: OwnerFormField retains a path with tuple positions
The field name alone is the complete location
Another model or page definition supplies the location
open_points.default_guess: Retain an explicit path, including tuple positions, as a fact of OwnerFormField.

witness.initial: An owner request contains two nested values whose leaf field is named `id`, one inside the request and one inside a tuple in its values.
events: The owner interface looks up the OwnerFormField row to construct the request.
outcomes: The row carries a path and selects the intended nested or tuple member.
The implementation guesses a location from the name and scope.
witness.observer: The product action receiving the request sees different facts populated.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField destination
open_points.text: whether it belongs to the owner's request itself or to the values the owner gives
open_points.question: What are the closed semantic destinations represented by this fact, and does it say where the parsed value is written or merely classify the field?
options: A closed two-value destination fact: request or values
A descriptive classification, with a separate destination/path fact
Page-specific destinations beyond request and values are allowed
open_points.default_guess: Make it a closed two-value destination fact and combine it with an explicit location.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField closed-list reading
open_points.text: as one of a closed list
open_points.question: For a field read from a closed list, what fact identifies the particular closed list whose member values are accepted?
options: Each such row references a declared enum or vocabulary
Each row embeds its permitted semantic values
There is one global closed list shared by all such fields
open_points.default_guess: Have each row reference a separately declared closed enum or vocabulary.

witness.initial: Two owner fields use different closed lists, such as customer kind and artifact type.
events: The owner selects a value in each form.
The owner interface reads both submitted texts using their OwnerFormField rows.
outcomes: Each row identifies its own closed list and produces a member of the correct domain.
Both rows expose only a generic closed-list reading kind, so the reader must guess which list applies.
witness.observer: The owner and the receiving product actions see different accepted values and model facts.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField row uniqueness
open_points.question: What makes two rows rows for the same field, and are duplicate names forbidden globally, forbidden only within a page or destination, or permitted when other facts differ?
options: Names are globally unique and duplicates make the release invalid
Names are unique within a page
The complete tuple of declared facts is the key and duplicate names are allowed
open_points.default_guess: Require globally unique names and reject a release containing duplicates.

witness.initial: The provider table contains two rows named `status`, one belonging to the request and one to its values.
events: A release containing both rows is assembled.
The owner interface looks up `status` while reading a submission.
outcomes: The release is invalid because a name must select exactly one row.
Both rows are valid and lookup requires additional facts.
witness.observer: The release builder and owner-interface reader see whether the release can be used deterministically.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField table completeness
open_points.question: Is the table a closed, exhaustive set of fields the owner interface may read, and what happens to a submitted or displayed field for which it has no row?
options: Only named rows are read; an unlisted submitted field is ignored
Every owner form field must have a row; a release missing one is invalid
Unlisted fields are read by a generic fallback
open_points.default_guess: Treat the table as exhaustive for readable fields and do not read an unlisted field.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField query fields
open_points.text:
what the
owner types or picks in a form
open_points.question: Does OwnerFormField also represent owner-page query inputs, or only form-body inputs?
options: Both form and query inputs are represented
Only form-body inputs are represented
Query inputs use a different model
open_points.default_guess: Include both form and query inputs in this model.

witness.initial: An owner list page has a query control for including archived records.
events: The browser submits it as a query parameter.
The owner interface attempts to read it.
outcomes: The query field has an OwnerFormField row and is read through the table.
The model covers only form inputs, so the query field is handled separately or not read.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether the requested list selection takes effect.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField creation authority and source
open_points.text: The release: the owner form table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: Which named data provider mints or authors OwnerFormField values, from which exact release artifact or constant, and can any other product action create or change them?
options: The data provider alone authors them in `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` for each release
The owner interface derives them from its pages
The release assembly derives them from another model or contract
open_points.default_guess: The data provider alone supplies them through the release constant `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS`; runtime product actions only read them.
